Lewis, Charles Short] title_full: A Latin Dictionary year: 1879 publisher: Clarendon Press metadata_status: identified edition_status: online-transcriptions-of-1879-work; print-not-collated citation_status: citation-ready-for-named-online-entries quote_status: selected-lexical-phrase-verified; no-ancient-passage-quotation source_relation: Paraphrased passage_surface: '#passages' --- # Lewis and Short — A Latin Dictionary ## Work and access Lewis, Charlton T., and Charles Short. *A Latin Dictionary*. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1879. The selected witnesses are the Scaife ATLAS and Alatius transcriptions linked below, consulted on 8 September 2026. Cite the headword, sense and actual online witness. This record does not claim collation of the complete printed dictionary or independent reading of every ancient passage cited by its editors. Its nineteenth-century comparative reconstructions are not adopted as present specialist consensus. ## Use and return The dictionary **sources** Latin semantic distinctions in [E2 Arbitration](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md) and [E3 Fides–Credere](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Their generated relations remain authorial register 3. The lexical evidence supplies particular attested senses and a recoverable citation chain; it does not derive the QL field or establish an institutional chronology. ## Selected lexical witnesses ### q001 — Fides: reliance and credibility **Paraphrase:** the entry connects *fides* with *fido* and distinguishes reliance upon someone or something, credibility and fidelity. Its testimony example cites Cicero, *Pro Sulla* 3.10; the relation of competence and justice to confidence cites *De officiis* 2.9.33. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *fides*, initial literal senses and transferred quality; [Scaife entry n18127](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionary-entries.atlas_v1:lat.ls.perseus-eng2-n18127/), selected entry text read 2026-09-08. The stringed-instrument homograph is separate. No exact Ciceronian quotation is promoted. ### q002 — Credo: lending, protection and confidence **Paraphrase:** the entry distinguishes lending, committing something to another's protection, confidence and belief. It gives *creditum* as a loan and cites Cato, *De agri cultura* 5.4 in its discussion of lending under an owner's authority. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *credo*, business use and transferred uses; [Scaife entry n11525](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionary-entries.atlas_v1:lat.ls.perseus-eng2-n11525/), selected senses read 2026-09-08. Cato's primary passage and the proposed deeper reconstruction retain independent collation tasks. E3's before/after-arbitration relation is not the dictionary's chronology. ### q003 — Natio: birth, kinds and peoples **Paraphrase:** the entry associates *natio* with *nascor*. Its uses range from birth through group or kind to peoples; examples also concern animals and things. Its political vocabulary does not define the modern nation-state. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *natio*, introductory morphology and senses I–II/B; [Alatius transcription](https://www.alatius.com/ls/index.php?met=up&ord=natio), read 2026-09-08. Primary contexts and the later history of national institutions are separate evidence tasks. ### q004 — Arbitrari: observation, weighing, judgment and credited testimony **Paraphrase:** *arbitror* carries observation into mental examination and weighing, then distinguishes judicial decision, testimony and opinion. The dictionary's judicial subsection records the exact lexical construction **“fidem alicui arbitrari”**, citing Plautus, *Bacchides* 3.6.41, for credit accorded to someone. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *arbitror*, I, II.A and II.B; [Alatius transcription](https://www.alatius.com/ls/index.php?met=up&ord=arbitror), full entry read 2026-09-08. The quoted four-word construction is verified as dictionary wording. It is not presented as a continuous quotation from an independently collated Plautus edition. E2's witness→weighing→decision distinction and the E3 Fides bridge now have this exact lexical witness; the ancient dramatic context remains to be recovered independently. ### q005 — Arbiter: witness and deciding office **Paraphrase:** the entry distinguishes a person present to see or hear from an appointed deciding office. Judicial uses include inquiry and settlement, followed by general judging and governing uses. Its selected examples concern boundary disputes and the distribution of an estate; these keep the object of judgment identifiable. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *arbiter*, introduction, I and II.A–C; [Alatius transcription](https://www.alatius.com/ls/index.php?l=arbiter), full entry read 2026-09-08. The dictionary's proposed going/coming derivation and historical account of Roman procedural change remain the editors' claims, requiring independent specialist collation before stronger use. The semantic distinction supports E2 without making witnessing and judging identical offices. ### q006 — Ratio — reckoning and rendering an account **Paraphrase:** The entry connects ratio with reor/ratus and distinguishes reckoning, account, calculation and computation. Its examples include receipts and expenditure and rendering an account. This attests the selected Latin semantic field; it does not verify a common ancestry with Greek arithmos or harmony. **Locator and verification:** s.v. ratio, introduction and literal accounting senses; https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionary-entries.atlas_v1:lat.ls.perseus-eng2-n40449/ ; selected senses read 2026-09-08, raw witness retained in T21-E6-private-development-packet.json. Paraphrase-ready to the online entry, with no independently verified ancient quotation or print collation. E6-ratio consumes this range while retaining A15’s native derivation and separate comparative-root debt. The entry **sources** [E6’s historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and its [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md), with the institutional relation at register 3.

--- title: Liddell–Scott–Jones — A Greek-English Lexicon (9th ed., 1940) source_id: lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon primary_domain: classical-philology node_type: source-house record_type: dictionary ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 author: - Henry George Liddell - Robert Scott - Henry Stuart Jones title_full: A Greek-English Lexicon year: 1940 edition: Ninth edition metadata_status: identified edition_status: selected-online-transcriptions; print-not-collated citation_status: citation-ready-for-named-online-entries quote_status: selected-senses-paraphrase-ready; no-exact-quotation source_relation: Paraphrased passage_surface: '#passages' --- # A Greek-English Lexicon Liddell, Henry George, and Robert Scott. *A Greek-English Lexicon*. Revised by Henry Stuart Jones with Roderick McKenzie. 9th ed. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1940. Selected LSJ entry transcriptions were read at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy’s CLD and Scaife ATLAS on 8 September 2026. Other dictionaries displayed on the same page retain separate authorship. Cite headword, sense and the actual transcription. Primary passages cited inside a lexicon are leads until independently collated. The source **sources** lexical distinctions in [E2 Arbitration](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md) and [E3 Fides–Credere](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Those fields’ generated operations remain authorial register 3. ## Selected lexical witnesses ### q001 — Topos **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes physical place, situated position, a passage in an author and a rhetorical topic. Aeschines 3.78 and Aristotle, Rhetoric 1358a14, are dictionary witnesses for distinct uses. These senses do not establish the authorial Arche-Topos compound or a mathematical theorem. **Locator:** s.v. τόπος, place/position, textual passage and rhetorical topic. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/τόπος). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q002 — Logos **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes reckoning, monetary accounts, account-giving, esteem, relation and mathematical ratio. Euclid V, definition 3, is cited for ratio. Their shared headword does not collapse their objects; the selected semantic range does not establish a complete philosophy of Logos. **Locator:** s.v. λόγος, LSJ I.1–4 and II.1–2. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/λόγος). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q003 — Nomos **Paraphrase:** The entry associates νόμος with νέμω and distinguishes customary usage from law or ordinance. The differently accented νομός has its own entry. This is lexical evidence, not proof of a compulsory pasture-to-state history or of the essay’s sixfold. **Locator:** s.v. νόμος, introduction and habitual practice/custom/law senses. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n71005/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q004 — Krisis **Paraphrase:** The entry derives the noun from κρίνω and distinguishes separating, judging, choosing and judicial proceedings. Its Aristotle Politics 1275a23 citation connects judgment and office within the cited civic context. The dictionary is the verified witness here; that Aristotelian passage has not been independently collated for this card. **Locator:** s.v. κρίσις, LSJ introductory and decision/judgment senses. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/κρίσις). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q005 — Hybris **Paraphrase:** The initial sense concerns overbearing violence and insolence; the Odyssey suitors supply several cited examples. The semantic witness is narrower than Taylor’s exact theorem of a local determination occupying its determining condition. That theorem retains authorial standing; the lexicon does not independently derive it. **Locator:** s.v. ὕβρις, LSJ initial violence/insolence sense. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/ὕβρις). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q006 — Anamnesis **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes calling to mind or recollection, reminders, a memorial sacrifice, and a separate lunar-return use. Its recollection citations include Plato, Phaedo 72e and 92d, Philebus 34c, and Aristotle, De memoria 451a21. These are dictionary witnesses; no complete Platonic argument is established by this card. **Locator:** s.v. ἀνάμνησις, introductory recollection sense and senses 2–3. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n7019/). **Verification:** entry read 2026-09-08; selected senses paraphrase-ready, ancient citation contexts and print edition not independently collated. **Consumer:** E2 recollection branch; the authorial return remains register 3. ### q007 — Homologia **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes agreement and verbal consistency; assent, admission and concession; and compacts, including terms of peace or surrender. Plato, Symposium 187b and Theaetetus 164c, Aristotle, Topics 110a33, and the historical treaty citations are lexical witnesses here, not independently collated primary passages. The semantic range does not establish that every agreement is true, freely made or an instance of QL homology. **Locator:** s.v. ὁμολογία, agreement, admission and compact senses, including the peace/truce/surrender sub-sense. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n73748/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 historical Greek branch and homological-agreement office; evidence register 2, with the authorial comparison at register 3. ### q008 — Analogia **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes mathematical and general proportion, analogy including grammatical analogy, relation, and correspondence or resemblance. Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics 1131a31, is a dictionary locator for the equality-of-ratios sense; Plato, Timaeus 31c–32c, is another cited witness. These primary passages were not independently collated. The range does not identify proportional analogy, focal predication and qualified predication as one historical doctrine. **Locator:** s.v. ἀναλογία, LSJ I–IV, including I.2 and II.2. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n6926/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08 from the Scaife entry, retrieved via HTTP after the browsing tool's open error; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 analogy/Greek branches and C63's differentiated comparison grammars; evidence register 2, with the authorial coordination at register 3. The agreement and proportion entries **source** [E5’s Greek historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#e5-greek). The corresponding [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD.md) retains the project’s operational comparison at register 3. ### q009 — Νέμω — distribution and holding a portion **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes distributing portions, assigning honour or privilege, and middle-voice holding as one’s portion. Examples concern meat, property and land. These are attested semantic offices; the dictionary citations are not independently collated primary passages and do not establish a single chronology from pasture to state. **Locator and verification:** s.v. νέμω, distributive active and possessive middle senses; https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.04.0057%3Aentry%3Dne%2Fmw ; read 2026-09-08, raw witness retained in T21-E6-private-development-packet.json. Paraphrase-ready to the online entry; print not collated. E6 branch E6-names consumes register-2 distribution/possession distinctions; its institutional return is register 3. The entry **sources** [E6’s historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and its [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md), with the institutional relation at register 3.

--- title: ATILF — TLFi, regard source_id: atilf-tlfi-regard primary_domain: language-literary-studies node_type: source-house record_type: dictionary-entry ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 metadata_status: identified citation_status: citation-ready-for-selected-transcription quote_status: source-matched-paraphrase; no-exact-quotation source_relation: Paraphrased passage_surface: '#passages' author: ATILF title_full: Trésor de la langue française informatisé, s.v. regard edition_status: CNRTL online etymology entry; dated source editions not independently collated url: https://www.cnrtl.fr/etymologie/regard --- # ATILF — TLFi, regard ATILF. *Trésor de la langue française informatisé*, s.v. “regard,” Étymologie et histoire. CNRTL. Consulted 8 September 2026. Cite the actual online entry; the portal’s copyright date does not date composition of each dictionary statement. The entry **sources** the French branch of [E2’s Regard operation](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md). English borrowing and Anglo-French history require their own witnesses. ## Lexical witness ### q001 — Looking, attention and administrative inspection **Paraphrase:** the entry treats *regard* as derived from *regarder* and dates ocular use to the late tenth century, attentive regard to the first half of the twelfth, inspection to 1262 and administrative control to 1464. It also records an opening for inspecting a fountain’s interior in 1580. **Locator and verification:** [CNRTL, regard, Étymologie et histoire](https://www.cnrtl.fr/etymologie/regard), full etymology section read 2026-09-08. The medieval and early modern editions cited there remain dictionary-mediated witnesses. These differentiated uses develop the French historical branch; they do not prove Taylor’s Con-text-through-Diaphaneity relation or supply an English first-use date.
